item.title: Was Don Lemon’s Arrest an Attack on Press Freedom?

item.title: Is the Coachella Valley Rail Project Worth the Cost and Wait?
item.description: After years of planning with little movement, the Coachella Valley Rail Project has cleared a key hurdle as the Riverside County Transportation Commission approved an $80 million contract to advance detailed planning and environmental work. item.title: Hero Of The Week : LifeStream Blood Bank
item.description: Community members throughout the Coachella Valley are responding to an urgent call for help by donating blood at Lifestream Blood Bank in Rancho Mirage, as January marks National Blood Donor Month. item.title: Could 450 Rats in a House Become a “Ratpocalypse”?
item.description: An unusual animal welfare situation on Long Island has drawn national attention as rescue workers report capturing approximately 450 domesticated white rats from an abandoned home—an infestation now nicknamed “Ratpocalypse.” The owner of the property reportedly failed to separate male and female rats, leading to continuous breeding cycles every 20 days. item.title: Why Did a Former Lawyer Trade the Courtroom for a Pie Shop in Palm Desert?
item.description: A new dessert destination is opening its doors in Palm Desert as Winston Pies, a Los Angeles-based bakery known for its handmade pies, expands into the Coachella Valley. The company was founded by Brianna Abrams, a former attorney who left her legal career to pursue her passion for baking full time. item.title: Jerry's SoCal Weather Briefing on Saturday, January 31, 2026!
item.description: The Coachella Valley will be under all sunshine this afternoon with above-normal high temperatures in the lower-80s.More lower-80s on Sunday with a few wispy high clouds followed by thicker fair-weather cirrus clouds and more above-normal midday temps in the lower-80s.You'll see sunny skies for your Tuesday with slightly warmer numbers in the middle-80s.@JerrySteffen @NBCPalmSprings For more Coachella Valley News visit NBCPalmSprings.com

item.title: Firebirds fall short to San Diego Friday night at Acrisure Arena
item.description: Coachella Valley rallied late in the third period to tie the game at 3, but San Diego scored the go-ahead goal to come away with two points in the desert. Our Tim O'Brien has the recap. For more Coachella Valley News visit NBCPalmSprings.com

item.title: Chef Said On A Plate
item.description: Personal chef and co-host of The Desert Brew, Chef Said, cooks us kafka with potatoes. We talk about his journey into food, his Lebanese roots and inspirations, his architectural design to plating, and of course his famous spice suitcase with flavors from all over the world. This is Chef Said on a plate. For more Coachella Valley News visit NBCPalmSprings.com

item.title: Signs of Fascism Rally Held in Indio Saturday
item.description: Democrats in Sun City Shadow Hills gathered Saturday morning for a protest aimed at raising awareness about what organizers call signs of fascism in the United States.The demonstration began around 10 a.m. in the Food 4 Less parking lot at the corner of Monroe Street and Highway 111 in Indio.
